recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-19376 unless PA later reopens the broader actor target-profile policy.
issue_request: FHIR-19376 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request asking Appointment to support PractitionerRole as well as Practitioner when a virtual appointment needs a practitioner's organizational affiliation or role. The recorded resolution was to update the reference options to include PractitionerRole for the appointment actor; in current source this is Appointment.participant.actor.
initial_application: Commit 87ce43db922810cf7461a4b098916209234ae0be on 2018-10-28 explicitly listed GF#19376 and changed the old Appointment spreadsheet source so Appointment.participant.actor accepted Reference(Patient|Practitioner|PractitionerRole|RelatedPerson|Device|HealthcareService|Location) instead of omitting PractitionerRole. Later source refactoring moved the authoritative input to structuredefinition-Appointment.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps Appointment and PractitionerRole in the active [resources] list and assigns Appointment to PA. Current Appointment.participant.actor includes PractitionerRole among its target profiles, and adjacent AppointmentResponse.actor and Schedule.actor definitions also include PractitionerRole. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later FHIR-core decision reversing or narrowing PractitionerRole support for Appointment.participant.actor.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current active Appointment source already implements the requested target profile, and adding redundant narrative or altering unrelated search parameters would exceed the scope of FHIR-19376.
